entries.topic: Religious institutions, both sides, added to the network map (Nov 2026)

claims.text: London Society founded 1809 by evangelical Anglicans (Wilberforce, Simeon); agenda included the physical restoration of the Jewish people; Jerusalem clinic 1836; Christ Church 1849; supported the 1841 bishopric, whose first bishop Michael Solomon Alexander was its worker.
Chief Rabbinate elected 24 Feb 1921 (Kook, Jacob Meir); Palestine Gazette 1 Apr 1921: government recognizes the Council as sole authority in Jewish law.

Pittsburgh Platform 1885: 'no longer a nation, but a religious community'; Columbus Platform 1937: 'the obligation of all Jewry to aid in its upbuilding as a Jewish homeland'; American Council for Judaism founded 1942.
Status quo letter, 19 June 1947, Ben-Gurion to Agudat Israel, four days after UNSCOP began its tour; Sabbath, kashrut, religious family law, school autonomy.

Jacob de Haan, representative of Rabbi Sonnenfeld's community, lobbied the British (Northcliffe 1922), planned a London delegation; shot 30 June 1924 by Haganah member Avraham Tehomi; Yosef Hecht testified in 1952 that he and the Jerusalem commander decided it.
